Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 76, verse 1:

(p-6008) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

Surah al-Insan

It is also called Surah al-Dahr, Surah al-Amshaj, and Surah Hal Ata. It is Meccan, and its verses number thirty-one.

Imam Muslim narrated from Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to recite in the Fajr prayer on Friday: "Alif Lam Mim, the Revelation (al-Sajdah)," and "Has there come upon man..." (Hal ata 'ala al-insan).

(p-6009) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

The discussion concerning the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying:

[1] ﴿Has there come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing worth mentioning?﴾

"Has there come upon man..." means: during that period. Rather, he was a forgotten thing, his sperm-drop being in the loins. The interrogative here is for affirmation (taqrir).

Al-Shihab said: That is, the question carries the sense of compelling them to affirm what the interrogative particle introduces, and the one being made to affirm is the one who denies resurrection. It is known that they would say, "Yes, a long age passed in which there was no human being." It is then said to them: He who brought them into existence after they were not, how could it be impossible for Him to bring them back to life after their death? The word "man" (al-insan) here refers to the species of the children of Adam.

The Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[2] ﴿Indeed, We created man from a sperm-drop mixed (nutfah amshaj), that We may test him; so We made him hearing and seeing.﴾

﴿Indeed, We created man from a sperm-drop mixed⁠—﴾ i.e., of various constituents (akhlat), namely its component substances composed of it. It is the plural of mashaj or mashij, like sabab and asbab, and nasir and ansar. Or it is a singular, like barmat a'shar: the barmah is the cooking pot, and a'shar means indefinite, as if it had become ten pieces. End of quote. ﴿That We may test him⁠—﴾ i.e., try him. The clause is in the position of a circumstantial state (hal), meaning: We created him as ones intending to test him, i.e., wishing to try him, not in vain or aimlessly. ﴿So We made him hearing and seeing⁠—﴾ i.e., so that We may see whether he turned his hearing and sight toward listening to the signs of Allah and contemplating them. And since the completion of the favour through these two lies in the bestowal of reason, he pointed to it with His words, glorified is He:

Discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[3] ﴿Indeed, We guided him to the way, whether he be grateful or ungrateful.﴾

﴿Indeed, We guided him to the way﴾ — that is, the way of good and evil, of salvation and destruction. That is, We made him know it and clarified it for him (p-6010) by the proofs of reason and revelation. ﴿Whether he be grateful﴾ — that is, by being guided and following it. ﴿Or ungrateful﴾ — that is, by turning away from it. Their accusative state is governed by an implied "yakūnu" (let it be), meaning: so that he might be either grateful or ungrateful; that is, so that his gratitude may be distinguished from his ingratitude, and his obedience from his disobedience, as in His words: ﴿that He may test you as to which of you is best in deed﴾ [al-Mulk: 2].

Al-Razi said: al-Qaffal said: The figurative sense of this expression under this interpretation is the saying of one who says: "I have advised you; if you wish, accept, and if you wish, leave it," meaning: "if you wish," with the fa' (then) elided. Likewise the meaning is: ﴿Indeed, We guided him to the way﴾, so [it is up to him:] whether grateful or ungrateful, the fa' being elided. It may also be understood as a warning, meaning: Indeed, We guided him to the way; so if he wills, let him disbelieve, and if he wills, let him be grateful; for indeed We have prepared for the disbelievers such-and-such, and for the grateful such-and-such. Like His words: ﴿And say: The truth is from your Lord, so whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve﴾ [al-Kahf: 29]. End of quotation.

A subtle point:

In (al-Nahr) it is said: Since gratitude is possessed by few, He said ﴿grateful (shākiran)﴾; and since disbelief is common, many people possess it, and its occurrence among humans is frequent, unlike gratitude, He said ﴿ungrateful (kafūran)﴾ in the intensive form (of hyperbole). End of quotation.

And this is more subtle than the view that it is based on observing the rhyme-endings of the verses.

The commentary on His words, may He be exalted:

[4] ﴿Indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers chains, and shackles, and a blazing Fire.﴾

﴿Indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers chains﴾, i.e., that they may be led by them and secured by them, tightly bound in the Hellfire. ﴿And shackles﴾, i.e., that their hands may be fastened in them to their necks. ﴿And a blazing Fire﴾, i.e., a fire that is kindled against them so that it blazes.

(p-6011)

The Discourse on the Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[5–6] ﴿Indeed, the righteous will drink from a cup whose mixture is of camphor﴾ ﴿a spring from which the servants of Allah drink; they make it gush forth in abundance﴾ [Al-Insan: 6]

﴿Indeed, the righteous﴾ — i.e., those who were dutiful (barru) to their Lord through their obedience, in performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions. ﴿will drink from a cup﴾ — i.e., wine (khamr), which is named by the cup because of its proximity (li-l-mujawarah). ﴿whose mixture is﴾ — i.e., that with which it is mixed. ﴿of camphor﴾ — Ibn Jarir said: meaning in the fragrance of its scent, like camphor. Since camphor is among the perfumes they enjoy, it is a metaphor (kinayah) for whatever is scented with a pleasant aroma.

﴿a spring from which the servants of Allah drink; they make it gush forth in abundance﴾ [Al-Insan: 6] — i.e., they cause it to flow from its sources in the gardens of Paradise, a joyful flowing, as a variety of delight in bliss. The word ʿaynan ("a spring") is in the accusative, governed by a verb like (yu'tawna, "they are given"), and the bāʾ in bihā ("from which") carries the meaning of min ("from"). His words, exalted is He:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[7] ﴿They fulfil the vow and fear a Day whose evil will be widespread.﴾

﴿They fulfil the vow﴾ is a resumptive clause (isti'naf) brought to explain the reason for which they were granted the bounties that were mentioned. It contains a kind of detailing of what the name "the righteous" (al-abrar) indicates in summary, as if it were said: What do they do to attain that lofty rank? So it is said: They fulfil what they have obligated upon themselves, so how about what Allah, exalted is He, has obligated upon them? ﴿And they fear a Day whose evil﴾ — that is, its punishment — ﴿will be widespread﴾, spreading out, manifest to the utmost degree.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 76, verse 8:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[8] ﴿And they give food, despite their love for it, to the needy, the orphan, and the captive.﴾

﴿And they give food, despite their love for it﴾ means: along with their love of food, like His saying: ﴿You will never attain righteousness until you spend from what you love﴾ [Al-Imran: 92]. Or it means: out of love for Allah, exalted is He, due to His saying that follows: ﴿for the sake of Allah's countenance﴾ [Al-Insan: 9]. ﴿To the needy, the orphan, and the captive﴾ means: the captive taken in war or for some public interest. He limited it to these three because they are among the most deserving of charity: the needy is incapable of earning what suffices him; the orphan has lost the one who supports him and earns for him, together with the utmost helplessness of his young age; and the captive has no power or means to help himself.

Al-Qasimi said in (al-Iklil): This verse indicates that feeding a polytheist is among the things by which one draws near to Allah, exalted is He, that is, due to His saying, glorified is He:

The discourse on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[9] ﴿Indeed, we feed you only for the sake of Allah. We do not want from you reward or gratitude.﴾

﴿Indeed, we feed you only for the sake of Allah﴾ meaning: saying this by the tongue of state or of speech, and to dispel the suspicion of reproach (mann), which invalidates charity, and the expectation of recompense. That is, we intend by feeding you only His reward, exalted is He, and nearness to Him and closeness in His presence. The use of "face" (wajh) for the essence is a well-known metaphor (majaz). ﴿We do not want from you reward﴾ meaning: repayment, ﴿nor gratitude﴾ meaning: praise and commendation.

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[10] ﴿Indeed, we fear from our Lord a Day, stern and distressing.﴾

﴿Indeed, we fear from our Lord a Day﴾ meaning: the punishment of a Day. ﴿Stern﴾ meaning: severe and dark. Or, the faces are contracted in it (ta'bis) because of the severity of its hardships and the length of its trial. ﴿Distressing﴾ meaning: extremely contracted and grievous. Their fear of the Day is a metaphor (kinayah) for doing righteous deeds that secure them from its terror and dread.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 76, verses 11–13:

The discussion of His saying, the Exalted:

[11–13] ﴿So Allah will protect them from the evil of that Day and give them radiance and happiness.﴾ ﴿And will reward them for what they patiently endured with a garden and silk.﴾ [Al-Insan: 12] ﴿Reclining therein on adorned couches; they will see therein neither sun nor bitter cold.﴾ [Al-Insan: 13]

(p-6013) ﴿So Allah will protect them from the evil of that Day﴾, i.e., because of what was mentioned of their fear of it. ﴿And will give them radiance﴾, i.e., in their faces, ﴿and happiness﴾, i.e., in their hearts.

﴿And will reward them for what they patiently endured﴾ [Al-Insan: 12], i.e., for their patience in obeying Allah, avoiding His prohibitions, calling to His way, and bearing harm. ﴿A garden and silk﴾ [Al-Insan: 12], i.e., they will wear it and adorn themselves with it.

﴿Reclining therein on adorned couches﴾ [Al-Insan: 13], i.e., the thrones (al-surur). ﴿They will see therein neither sun nor bitter cold﴾ [Al-Insan: 13], i.e., neither heat nor cold, by way of mentioning the necessary concomitant (al-malzum) and intending the consequence (al-lazim).

Commentary on the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[14–16] ﴿And near over them will be its shade, and its fruits will be made easy to reach, made fully accessible.﴾ ﴿And there will be circulated among them vessels of silver and goblets that were glass–﴾ [Al-Insan: 15] ﴿glass of silver, which they have determined in measure.﴾ [Al-Insan: 16]

﴿And near over them will be its shade﴾: that is, the shade of its trees, meaning close to them, providing shade over them, as an increase in their bliss. ﴿And its fruits will be made easy to reach, made fully accessible﴾: that is, its fruits will be made easy for those who reach for them, so distance and thorns will not keep their hands away from them.

﴿And there will be circulated among them vessels of silver and goblets﴾ [Al-Insan: 15]: "Goblets" (akwab) is the plural of "kub" (kub), which is a cup with no handle. ﴿That were glass﴾ [Al-Insan: 15]; ﴿glass of silver﴾ [Al-Insan: 16]. Abu al-Baqa said: the repetition is good because of what is connected to it, the explanation of their origin. Had there been no repetition, it would not have been good for the first (qawarir) to be the end of a verse, due to the strong connection of the attribute to the thing described. ﴿Which they have determined in measure﴾ [Al-Insan: 16]: that is, within themselves they intended that they be of measures and shapes according to their desires. So they came as they had determined, or the cupbearers determined them for them according to the measure of their thirst, neither more nor less. And this is more pleasant for the drinker, since it is according to the measure of his need: it is not in excess, nor does it fall short.

Abu Hayyan said: Closer to this is what Abu Hatim suggested, namely that the original was "qaddara riyyahum minha taqdiran" (he measured their quenching of thirst from it), and "al-riyy" means quenching of thirst. So the genitive-dependent noun was omitted, along with the preposition, and the verb was made to reach its object directly.

Al-Shihab said: As for whether this is closer, there is room for consideration, since it is more forced. But "every party rejoices in what is with them" (Qur'an 23:53).

(p-6014)

The commentary on His saying, exalted is He:

[17–18] ﴿And they will be given to drink therein a cup whose mixture is of ginger﴾ ﴿a spring therein named Salsabil﴾ [al-Insan: 18]

﴿And they will be given to drink therein a cup whose mixture is of ginger﴾, i.e., something resembling it in taste. The Arabs used to delight in drinks mixed with it (ginger).

﴿a spring therein named Salsabil﴾ [al-Insan: 18]. It is a spring of intense flow, flowing with a particular, delightful kind of smoothness. The accusative of "ʿaynan" (a spring) is governed by a verb like (they will be given, yu'tawna) or (they will look upon, yanẓurūna).

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[19] ﴿And there will go around them young boys made eternal. When you see them, you would think them scattered pearls.﴾

﴿And there will go around them young boys made eternal﴾ That is: they do not die. Or: their youth is lasting, and they do not change from that age. Or: they are adorned with bracelets (musawwarun). Or: they wear earrings (muqarratun).

﴿When you see them, you would think them scattered pearls﴾ That is: because of their beauty and their number in their places, and their dispersal throughout their dwellings and places.

The Explanation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[20–21] ﴿And when you look there, you will see bliss and a great dominion﴾ ﴿Upon them will be garments of green fine silk and brocade, and they will be adorned with bracelets of silver, and their Lord will give them a pure drink to drink﴾ [al-Insan: 21]

﴿And when you look there﴾, i.e., you gaze upon Paradise and cast your sight over what the righteous (al-abrar) have been given, ﴿you will see bliss and a great dominion﴾, i.e., vast, such that the sight cannot reach its limit.

﴿Upon them will be garments of green fine silk﴾ [al-Insan: 21]. Sundus is what is thin of silk. ﴿Green﴾ [al-Insan: 21]: it is read with raf' (nominative) for "thiyab" (garments) and with jarr (genitive) for "sundus". ﴿And brocade﴾ [al-Insan: 21]: it is what is thick of dibaj (figured silk). In it there are two readings, raf' and jarr. ﴿And they will be adorned with bracelets of silver, and their Lord will give them a pure drink to drink﴾ [al-Insan: 21], i.e., it is not filthy like the wine of this world. Or, because it has not been pressed, so that defiled hands do not touch it, nor do unclean feet tread upon it, nor is it placed in jars that have not been cared to be cleaned. This verse is among those used as evidence regarding the impurity of wine, because of the allusion to it contained therein.

The Interpretation of His Words, may He be exalted:

[22] ﴿Indeed, this is a reward for you, and your striving has been appreciated.﴾

﴿Indeed, this﴾, i.e., what has been enumerated of their reward, ﴿is a reward for you﴾, i.e., in return for the righteous deeds you had sent forward, ﴿and your striving has been appreciated﴾, i.e., it has been recompensed, not wasted.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 76, verse 23:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[23] ﴿Indeed, it is We who have sent down to you the Qur'an, sent down [in gradual revelation].﴾

﴿Indeed, it is We who have sent down to you the Qur'an, sent down [in gradual revelation].﴾ That is, [it is] great, its worth cannot be measured; that is, its command is true and its promise is sincere. The purpose is to strengthen his heart, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, to expand his breast, to confirm that what was sent down is revelation, and to disregard their throwing at him [the accusations of] sorcery and soothsaying.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[24] ﴿So be patient for the decree of your Lord, and do not obey from among them a sinner or a disbeliever.﴾

﴿So be patient for the decree of your Lord﴾, i.e., in proclaiming it, conveying its verses, and acting upon its commands. ﴿And do not obey from among them a sinner or a disbeliever﴾, i.e., do not obey, in disobedience to Him, Exalted is He, any of the polytheists of Makkah who commits sin and openly disbelieves, one who seeks to turn you away from returning from your call, by whatever you wish of wealth or demand. The "or" (aw) may be in its own sense: i.e., do not obey whoever possesses one of these two attributes. The prohibition against one in whom both are combined is known by the more evident reasoning. Or it may have the meaning of "and" (waw).

Al-Farra' said:

"Here 'aw' has the status of 'waw' (and). In negation, interrogation and conditional clauses it may carry the meaning of 'la' (not). This is of that kind, with negation." End of quotation.

Or it may have the meaning of "bal" (rather), a shift to a description that is more fitting and more deserving of him. Or it may be for choice in naming: i.e., whichever you wish, call him "the sinner" or "the disbeliever," since the meaning of each of them is realized in him.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[25–26] ﴿And mention the name of your Lord morning and evening﴾ ﴿And of the night, prostrate to Him and glorify Him through the long night﴾ [al-Insan: 25–26]

﴿And mention the name of your Lord﴾, i.e., by invoking Him, glorifying Him, and praying to Him, ﴿morning and evening﴾. ﴿And of the night, prostrate to Him﴾ [al-Insan: 26], i.e., by performing tahajjud (voluntary night prayer, prayer offered after sleeping at night) during it. ﴿And glorify Him through the long night﴾ [al-Insan: 26], i.e., for a long portion of it, half of it or more than half. In these commands, together with the command at the beginning of al-Muzzammil (Surah 73) and similar commands, there is an indication of the importance given to standing in prayer at night (qiyam al-layl) and of eagerness for it.

The discussion above also applies here, namely whether the command is specific to him, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, on the basis that it is for obligation, or whether it includes others by implication, the command being for the common measure. There are two well-known opinions regarding its counterpart. The purpose is to urge him, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, to seek help in calling his people and in openly proclaiming what he was commanded, through patience in bearing their harm and through prayer and glorification. This has been mentioned frequently in various passages of the Revelation, such as His saying: ﴿And seek help through patience and prayer﴾ [al-Baqarah: 45], and His saying:

﴿So be patient over what they say, and glorify your Lord with praise before the rising of the sun and before its setting﴾ [Qaf: 39], ﴿And during the night glorify Him, and after the prostrations﴾ [Qaf: 40], and similar verses.

(p-6017)

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[27] ﴿Indeed, these love the immediate (world) and leave behind them a heavy Day.﴾

﴿Indeed, these﴾, i.e., the polytheists, ﴿love the immediate﴾, i.e., the immediate pleasures, so they strive for them with all their effort, even if they destroy the tilth and the offspring. ﴿And leave behind them a heavy Day﴾, i.e., a severe one, due to the heaviness of its reckoning, its intensity and its hardship.

The Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[28] ﴿We created them and strengthened their joints; and when We will, We can replace their likes with a complete replacement.﴾

﴿We created them and strengthened their joints⦆ That is: their creation and the structure of their limbs.

Al-Shihab said: The root meaning of al-asr (the joints/binding) in the lexicon is tightening so that something becomes strong, and it is also applied to that with which something is tied and bound. For this reason the prisoner (al-asir) was named asir, meaning "bound." The sinews are likened to the ropes with which things are bound, so that the body is strengthened by them, or so that they hold the limbs together; for this reason they are also called ribat (ligaments).

﴿And when We will, We can replace their likes with a complete replacement⦆ That is: by destroying them and bringing others in their place. This is the focal point of the warning, and what precedes it serves as its justification.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[29] ﴿Indeed, this is a reminder, so whoever wills may take to his Lord a way.﴾

﴿Indeed, this﴾ — i.e., the surah, or the nearby verses — ﴿is a reminder﴾ — i.e., an admonition for whoever takes heed and is warned. ﴿So whoever wills may take to his Lord a way﴾ — i.e., through obedience that leads to nearness to Him, and by making the way a means of reaching the goals. This is a figurative expression (tamthil).

(p-6018)

The Explanation of His Words, may He be exalted:

[30–31] ﴿And you do not will except that Allah wills. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.﴾ ﴿He admits whom He wills into His mercy; but the wrongdoers—He has prepared for them a painful punishment.﴾ [al-Insan: 31]

﴿And you do not will except that Allah wills﴾. Ibn Jarir said: That is, you do not will to take the path to your Lord except that Allah wills that for you, because the matter is in His hands, not yours. That is, what Allah does not will to occur from the servant does not occur from the servant, and what He wills to occur from him does occur. This is equivalent to the saying: "What Allah wills occurs, and what He does not will does not occur." This is the interpretation of the early generation (al-Salaf). The Mu'tazilah said: That is, you do not will obedience except that Allah wills it by compelling them to it. The matter is elaborated in the discussions of theology (al-Kalam), and we have summarized it in our commentary on "Lu/tat al-'Ajlan" (Sharh Luqtat al-'Ajlan), so refer to it.

﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing﴾, that is, of their circumstances and what will come from them, ﴿Wise﴾, that is, in His management, His creation, and His command.

﴿He admits whom He wills into His mercy﴾ [al-Insan: 31]. Abu al-Su'ud said: It is an explanation of the firmness of His will, which follows from His knowledge and wisdom. That is, He admits into His mercy whomever He wills to admit into it, and He is the One who directs His will toward taking the path to Him, by granting him success in what leads to entering Paradise, namely faith and obedience.

﴿But the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Insan: 31], and they are those who turned their will toward the opposite of what has been mentioned, ﴿He has prepared for them a painful punishment﴾ [al-Insan: 31], meaning the punishment of the Fire. May Allah protect us from it by His bounty and generosity.
